questions.prompt: Who owns the repository interface, and who implements it?

options.text: The database owns it; the use case implements it
The use-case layer owns it (in domain terms); an outer gateway adapter implements it with the actual database code
The framework owns and implements it

questions.explanation: The inner use-case layer owns the repository interface phrased in domain terms; the outer gateway implements it and is the only place SQL/ORM lives.

questions.prompt: What does 'the database is a detail' mean?

options.text: Databases are unimportant and should be avoided
Storage is an outer, replaceable concern the business rules shouldn't depend on, and its choice can be deferred and changed
The database is the core of the system
You must use a NoSQL database

questions.explanation: The database is a tool for storing and retrieving data — an outer detail. Business rules shouldn't know or care which database is used.

questions.prompt: The pattern where a class is BOTH a domain object and its own database row (with .save() on it) — coupling the domain to the DB — is called ______ ______.
questions.explanation: Active Record fuses the domain to the database. Clean Architecture prefers the Data Mapper style, where domain objects are persistence-ignorant.

questions.prompt: Match each persistence term to its description.

pairs.right: An interface owned by the use-case layer, phrased in domain terms
Moves data between domain objects and the database, keeping them independent
A class that is both a domain object and its own database row
A domain object with no knowledge of how it is stored

questions.explanation: Clean Architecture prefers Data Mapper with persistence-ignorant domain objects behind a repository interface, rather than Active Record, which couples the domain to the database.

questions.prompt: Which belong in the gateway rather than in a use case or entity? Select all that apply.

options.text: The enterprise business rule the entity enforces

questions.explanation: SQL, ORM calls, and row↔object mapping all live in the gateway. The business rule stays in the entity.

questions.prompt: Order the steps a gateway takes to save an entity to a SQL database.

items.text: Receive the domain object via the repository interface
Map the domain object to a storage row
Return control to the use case

questions.explanation: The gateway receives a domain object, maps it to a row, runs the SQL, and returns — keeping all storage detail out of the use case.
